title: Anthony Albanese proposes national celebration in support of Socceroos
text:

Four people have been charged and police have seized multiple flares as the Socceroos end their world cup bid in a heartbreaking penalty shootout.

In a statement, Victoria Police said the arrests were made across two live sites as tens of thousands of fans braved a cold winter morning to cheer on the Socceroos in what would prove to be their final game in the 2026 World Cup.

Around 7500 people gathered at Federation Square, where 11 flares and one smoke emitter were activated during the match.

Six of those flares were lit and thrown immediately after Australia equalised at one-all as fans celebrated an own goal by Egyptian defender Mohammed Hany.

During the incident Victoria Police say one man was arrested for possessing a distress signal and discharging a missile, while three others were arrested for flare possession.

A teenager was also arrested for possessing a flare, but was released pending further inquiries.

In Victoria it is an offence to carry or ignite a flare under the Dangerous Goods (explosives) Act.

In a separate gathering around 6000 fans attended a live site in AAMI park where police say two people were found with weapons by security at the entrance to the venue. They were both issued penalty notices.

Two others were directed to leave the venue after entering the pitch.

All four were released and are expected to be charged on summons.

Despite the arrests, police said they were generally pleased with crowd behaviour and shared their sympathy with the crowd following a disappointing penalty shootout.

The Socceroos World Cup bowed out of the 2206 FIFA World Cup in a dramatic penalty shootout, after extra time was unable to split Australia and Egypt.

Socceroos star Jackson Irvine summed up the mood of many fans as he reflected on the teams cruel exit from the 2026 World Cup.

“We took it all the way to the very end,” he said on SBS.

“Penalties, it’s a cruel way to lose, but anybody who’s got the confidence to step up and take that ball after 120 minutes, however long you’ve played, it takes a big heart.”

‘Week off’ joke

A week off for Australians is off the agenda after the Socceroos’ devastating loss to Egypt in the FIFA World Cup early on Saturday morning.

Anthony Albanese had teased Australians could be granted a week off if we won the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

But that came to an end with a brutal penalty shootout in Dallas on Saturday morning, after the Socceroos and Egypt ended extra time 1-1.

“Heartbreaking way to exit the World Cup after a great tournament – all Australians are proud of our @Socceroos,” the Prime Minister posted on X shortly after pre-dawn loss.

On Friday, after delivering the keynote address at the Airport City Summit, Mr Albanese had playfully joked about giving the country a week off if the Socceroos won the World Cup.

“The truth is that public holidays are completely determined by state governments,” he said.

“But I reckon if we win then we might give everyone a week.”

Thousands of Aussies showed up at live sites and bars and pubs around the country for the knockout round game, which started at 4am AEST.

Millions more were expected to watch from home.

Some betting companies had the Socceroos at a 300-1 chance of winning the World Cup, according to UK based company Squawka.

The event, hosted by the Western Sydney Leadership Dialogue, explored how the new Western Sydney Airport will support new infrastructure and investment opportunities.

The Prime Minister used his keynote to promote the Socceroos, saying they represent the vision of a multicultural Australia.

“We’re a multicultural nation. It’s who we are, and you know what? We should celebrate. The Socceroos show that, and the pride,” he said.

“We should be proud of it, and we should celebrate it, just as we’ll celebrate every Socceroo, whether their name is Irankunda or Irvine, they’re all just proud to be representing our country, but they’re also proud of who they are.”

Originally published as Four arrested in Melbourne after Socceroos heartbreaking World Cup loss
